"It is a way to take people's wealth from them without having to openly raise taxes. Inflation is the most universal tax of all." - Thomas Sowell

Video: https://t.co/jzfV3acG3j https://t.co/M2tDfOcf46
hits.hook: "It is a way to take people's wealth from them without having to openly raise taxes. Inflation is the most universal tax of all." - Thomas Sowell
hits.draft_en:
Inflation is a tax, and not only in the Sowell sense.

The tax code taxes it directly. Capital gains are measured in nominal dollars, with no adjustment for inflation. Buy an asset for $100,000, sell it years later for $130,000 after prices rose 30%, and the $30,000 gain is taxable even though your purchasing power didn't grow at all.

Tax brackets get indexed for inflation every year. Cost basis never does.
hits.video_tip: Talking-head, 30 seconds: hold up two index cards, '$100k bought' and '$130k sold', then flip the second to show '$100k in today's dollars'.

-Operating Expenses in first half: $17.0 billion, up 415% YoY

hits.hook: Anthropic S-1:
hits.draft_en:
Anthropic's S-1 shows an $80.8B net loss on $16.3B of revenue. Most of that loss never left the bank account.

Here's how that happens. When a company issues convertible notes and carries them at fair value, every rise in its valuation raises what the notes are worth. That increase is booked as a loss on the income statement. No cash moves.

So a company getting more valuable can make its reported loss bigger. Read cash flow from operations before you read net income.
hits.video_tip: 40-second whiteboard: draw two columns, 'net income' and 'cash', write the $80.8B loss in one and a small number in the other, then draw the arrow from 'valuation up' to 'note liability up'.

Only two of the Mag 7 stocks are outperforming the market this year:

Apple and Nvidia.

What do they have in common?

They rank #1 and #2 in free cash flow.

Investors are rewarding cash generation and growing more skeptical of massive AI spending with uncertain future returns. https://t.co/lj4QOle7Rl
hits.hook: Only two of the Mag 7 stocks are outperforming the market this year:
hits.draft_en:
Only two Mag 7 stocks are beating the market this year, and they rank #1 and #2 in free cash flow. That's an accounting lesson as much as a market one.

Earnings spread the cost of a data center over its useful life through depreciation. Free cash flow subtracts the full capex the year the check is written.

When capex surges, earnings can look fine while free cash flow shrinks. Investors seem to have noticed which number is harder to dress up.
hits.video_tip: 45-second screen recording: put one company's net income and free cash flow lines on the same chart and pause where they split as capex ramps.
